delay_duration_stated: Awarded Jan 2018, appointed date fixed only June 2019
source_report: CAG Report No.19 of 2023 (Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I Performance Audit)
summary: Project was foreclosed once already under the earlier NHDP scheme (2013) for the same reason before being re-awarded under Bharatmala; right-of-way was still not fully handed over even after the appointed date, forcing part of the route to be dropped and part to remain under arbitration, leaving it at 61.6% progress well past its original completion date.

delay_duration_stated: Awarded Jan 2018, Stage-I forest clearance received Sept 2018, appointed date Nov 2019
source_report: CAG Report No.19 of 2023 (Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I Performance Audit)
summary: Route passes through a wildlife sanctuary area; forest clearance alone took roughly eight months after award, and combined with other right-of-way issues pushed the construction start date to almost two years after the project was awarded.

delay_duration_stated: Not awarded at all as of March 2023 due to pending forest clearance
source_report: CAG Report No.19 of 2023 (Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I Performance Audit)
summary: The adjoining half of the same original stretch as C002 could not even be awarded because its forest clearance was still pending, illustrating that a single unresolved clearance can stall a project indefinitely rather than just delay it.

delay_duration_stated: Not approved by CCEA in 2014 for lack of ROW; re-awarded March 2018; appointed date Dec 2019
source_report: CAG Report No.19 of 2023 (Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I Performance Audit)
summary: Right-of-way problems blocked this project from even being approved in its first attempt in 2014; after re-approval and award under Bharatmala, the same issue persisted and pushed the construction start almost two years past the award date, leaving it at 70% progress a year after its scheduled completion.

source_report: CAG Report No.19 of 2023 (Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I Performance Audit)
summary: A smaller bypass segment split off from C004 for separate execution, still showing the same right-of-way-driven gap between award and construction start, and still only 40.5% complete a year later.

delay_duration_stated: Baseline Socio-Economic survey for Phase I still incomplete 11+ years after Sept 2012; Project Affected Persons not rehabilitated as of Jan 2024
source_report: CAG Audit Report No. 2 of 2025 (Railways Compliance Audit)
summary: Resettlement housing for project-affected families was still not built by the responsible development authority more than a decade after the baseline survey began, which in turn blocked possession of land; a separate internal land-transfer request between two zones of the same railway had also gone unresolved for eight years.

delay_duration_stated: Land notifications issued 2006-2010; compensation award issued only 2009-2011; work completed May 2012
source_report: CAG Audit Report - PSUs for the year ended 31 March 2014 (Karnataka)
column15: Compensation for acquired land was awarded two to four years after the initial acquisition notification, and the contractor could not get a clear site until compensation was settled, stretching a 12-month contract into a six-year delay.

implementing_agency: Andhra Pradesh government / Polavaram Project Authority
delay_duration_stated: Cost revision of ~Rs 39538.42 crore proposed due to enhanced LARR compensation and under-estimated land requirement; revised cost pending GoI approval as of March 2023
source_report: CAG Performance Audit Report on Polavaram Irrigation Project (2025)
summary: The original cost estimate significantly under-provided for both the amount of land needed and the higher compensation rates mandated by the 2013 land acquisition law, producing one of the largest documented cost escalations directly attributable to land acquisition and compensation planning errors.

delay_duration_stated: 407.37 acres requisitioned; Rs 36.75 crore compensation undeposited as of Nov 2020 pending government fund approval; only 74% complete as of March 2022
source_report: CAG Report on Execution of Kaleshwaram Project (2024)
summary: Land had been formally requisitioned but the department itself had not released the compensation funds because government approval for the funds was still pending, stalling acquisition even though the landowners were not the source of the delay.

delay_duration_stated: Performance audit covering 2012-2017; project originally approved decades earlier and still incomplete
source_report: CAG Maharashtra Economic Sector Audit Report (tabled 28 March 2018)
summary: One of India's longest-running unfinished irrigation projects; audit scrutiny found land acquisition work was not properly coordinated with the survey and design process, contributing to a project timeline stretching over three decades.
